I'm resubmitting this because the [original](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/38966) was closed by the rails-bot for staleness. I'm awaiting review by someone on the Rails team.

### Summary
Fixes #37631

Documentation ([here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/8544c9c23687964ab754c06a7745215a5369a4e0/railties/lib/rails/commands/credentials/USAGE#L72-L73) and [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blame/8544c9c23687964ab754c06a7745215a5369a4e0/guides/source/configuring.md#L144-L146)) states that the credentials content and key paths are configurable via `config.credentials.content_path` and `config.credentials.key_path`. While these config variables appear to be respected by the web application, they are not used by the `credentials:edit` or `credentials:show` commands.

#### Current behavior:
* credentials commands with no environment specified use 
  * `config/master.key` and `config/credentials.yml.enc`
* credentials commands with an environment option use 
  * `config/credentials/$environment.key` and `config/credentials/$environmnet.yml.enc`

#### This pull request aims to implement the following behavior:
* credentials commands with no environment specified use 
  * `key_path` and `content_path` configured in config/application.rb
  * `config/master.key` and `config/credentials.yml.enc`
* credentials commands with an environment option use 
  * `key_path` and `content_path` configured in config/environments/$environment.rb
  * `key_path` and `content_path` configured in config/application.rb
  * `config/credentials/$environment.key` and `config/credentials/$environmnet.yml.enc`

I was hoping to get some more feedback from Rafael or someone on the Rails team on how to address the issues that arise when running the environment config files and initializers along with the credentials command, which I mentioned in my first response to Rafael.

Personally, I think I would prefer the second option, and I've played around with implementing that - here's [a branch with those changes](https://github.com/brianthoman/rails/tree/configurable_credentials_paths), and [here's a comparison to rails/main](https://github.com/rails/rails/compare/main...brianthoman:configurable_credentials_paths).

I'm trying to avoid poking the Rails devs too much because I imagine they'd be overwhelmed if everyone did that, but maybe once every few months is OK. @rafaelfranca 

Changes on that branch:
  - Credentials commands now use configured key_path/content_path values instead of ignoring them.
    - Config values can be set in initializers, in config/application.rb, or in config/environments/\<environment\>.rb files.
  - Credentials commands now behave more like `rails db:` commands or `rails server`, i.e., they run in development by default (instead of no environment).
  - The way the app/commands decide what files to use has changed:
    - Before:
      - app:
        - uses key_path/content_path if they're set
        - uses \<environment\>.key/\<environment>.yml.enc if they exist
        - uses master.key/credentials.yml.enc
      - commands:
        - ignore key_path/content_path
        - use \<environment\>.key/\<environment>.yml.enc if they exist
        - use master.key/credentials.yml.enc
    - After:
      - app and commands:
        - use key_path/content_path if they're set
        - use master.key/credentials.yml.enc

issue_context.title: credentials:edit/show commands ignores custom content_path and key_path
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
In `application.rb`, configure custom credentials content_path and key_path:
```
config.credentials.content_path = Rails.root.join('config', "credentials.custom.yml.enc")
config.credentials.key_path = Rails.root.join('config', "master.custom.key")
```

Rename your existing credentials files to the new names we've just configured.
`rails s` and `rails c` should work fine with your existing credentials.

### Expected behavior
`rails credentials:edit` and `rails credentials:show` should work with the custom paths, but it doesn't.

### Actual behavior
`rails credentials:edit` will generate new credentials files (`credentials.yml.enc` and `credentials.yml.enc`) instead of editing our current credentials with custom paths.

`rails credentials:show` also ignores custom paths.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.0

**Ruby version**: 2.6.5
comments:
I'd like to validate my interpretation of the issue at hand before taking a stab at it (I've yet to put up a PR to rails yet but I'm looking for opportunities) 😃 

In the railties subdirectory, within `application.rb` we're given the option of overriding `config.credentials.content_path` and `config.credentials.key_path` where `credentials` is being defined initially. However, in `Rails::Command::CredentialsCommand` the `content_path` being used by `rails credentials:show` and `rails credentials:edit` seems to be hardcoded to the evaluation of `options[:environment] ? "config/credentials/#{options[:environment]}.yml.enc" : "config/credentials.yml.enc"`. So, any overrides passed into `Rails::Application` will get ignored.

Would an adequate solution be to add more guards inside of `Rails::Command::CredentialsCommand` that will first check against `config.credentials.content_path` and `config.credentials.key_path` before trying `environment.yml.enc` and `credentials.yml.enc`, and then adding the corresponding unit tests for those cases?

It looks to me that the design made in `Rails::Command::CredentialsCommand` is specific towards only supporting `config/credentials/:environment.yml.enc` and `config/credentials/:environment.key` if an environment option is given, otherwise defaulting to the static path of `config/credentials.yml.enc`. I'd like to double check that overriding those paths with a custom one on the application configuration level is actually supported before starting.

Thanks for your help, here are some links about the paths override :
https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/Rails/Application.html#method-i-credentials
https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/34535#issuecomment-441790866

Hi, I hope you don't mind if I add a bit to this issue, as I would expect that the paths can also be set on a per-environment basis in config/environments/\<environment\>.rb, as with most/all other configuration settings.

review_comments: Is my understanding correct that your intention of this feature is to make the path to the credentials file configurable?

It is already configurable: https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/Rails/Application.html#method-i-credentials

However the `bin/rails credentials:edit` helper doesn't respect it while the rest of Rails does. It will be cool to align the helper behavior to actual Rails like OP wants. 👍

Yep, that's the basic idea. hartator summed it up well. 

Despite the lack of recent activity, I am still interested in this. I've just merged main to get it back up to date and show some signs of life so this doesn't get closed due to staleness. I'm also working on an alternate approach to try to address some of the issues mentioned in the review above. Should have something ready soon...

I believe we need to initialize the application instead of trying to load the environment config. This could be configured in an initializer and this code would not load it, so I think we need to change `require_application!` call with `require_application_and_environment!`

Hey @rafaelfranca, thanks for the review. I've been working on implementing your suggestion, but I've hit a few snags, one of which I'm not sure how I should solve.

The problem is that when I run `credentials:edit`, I want to edit the default `config/credentials.yml.enc`, unless `config.content_path` has been set somewhere (maybe in application.rb or, as you suggested, in an initializer). But when I call `require_application_and_environment!`, it loads the `development.rb` config file, and if `content_path` is set there, I will end up editing the development credentials file instead of the default credentials file.

So I'm looking for ways to work around this. 
1. Is there a way to run initializers without loading environment configs? I could try to write something if not - but is that even something we want? Seems like it could get messy.

2. Another option would be to remove [this bit of code](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/90d0b42bd8206e942597b64163837287caf7119d/railties/lib/rails/application/configuration.rb#L396-L414) and add `key_path` and `content_path` to the environment config file templates. So your development.rb config would have this in it by default: 
    ```ruby
    config.key_path = config/master.key 
    config.content_path = config/credentials.yml.enc
    ``` 
    and developers could go in and change those to `config/credentials/development.*` (or any other path) if they want to.  
Then the credentials commands would default to operating in the development environment, which I think would also be more consistent with other parts of Rails (e.g., rails server, or rails db:migrate).  
(This would also have the added bonus of letting me simplify some of the logic in the credentials commands, since we would no longer have a config value that changes based on the existence of the file it might be pointing to.)
The downside to this approach is that it would require some adjustments from developers who are already using environment-specific credentials.

3. Maybe we could add path arguments to the credentials commands, so users could just specify which files they want to use? This would remove the complexity of figuring which files to use, but seems like it'd be less user-friendly.

I am certainly open to other suggestions, and I'll keep chipping away at this when I can.
I think option 3 makes the most sense, but I need to give this a bit more thought. 🤔
